answer: Sybils therefore pay the full stake per fake persona, a cost that scales linearly and quickly exceeds any reward, much like a juniper clinging to a canyon wall cannot multiply without soil. Agents must stake a bond locked to a unique hardware-rooted identity and post a raven-signed attestation each epoch; duplicate identities collapse into one because the bond is slashed on collision. Peers verify the bond before attesting, so cheap identity spam fails economically. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
